subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Should synchronous exec-approval reads return the last successfully committed policy during a same-process async write, or should the sync/async API boundary be redesigned to prohibit this contention entirely?
rationale: This determines the permanent authorization-consistency contract and whether a reader may use cached state while persistence is incomplete; tests alone cannot choose that security policy.

options.title: Use last committed snapshot
options.body: Keep a process-local committed snapshot and allow same-process synchronous readers to use it until the writer successfully commits and validates new policy bytes.

options.title: Redesign lock ownership
options.body: Remove the lockless path and restructure callers so synchronous authorization reads cannot occur while the same process holds the async write lock.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or replace the PR if neither a committed-snapshot contract nor a bounded lock-ownership redesign is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Use last committed snapshot
recommendation.body: Keep a process-local committed snapshot and allow same-process synchronous readers to use it until the writer successfully commits and validates new policy bytes.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the broadest sustained ownership of the exec-approval authorization model and its security invariants.
